title: The 2026 Rookie Draft: The Roast, Uncut
intro: Forty-eight picks, five trades, one ghost, and nine years of receipts. The Oracle read every trade you've ever made, every point you've ever benched, and every message in the chat — including the ACT-exam saga — and has decided you should all hear the truth at full volume. This league traded away Josh Allen, Patrick Mahomes, Justin Herbert, and Cooper Kupp, and then had the balls to spend a Saturday grading ROOKIES. Fine. Let's grade.

1.blurb: Tim went 1-27, took the league-mandated ACT with a spreadsheet of colleges like a 34-year-old junior, audibly told a trig question 'fuck you,' got carded for hazy IPAs at the testing center — and then named his actual newborn son Jeremiayah Love a month before drafting Jeremiyah Love 1.01. The first pick in league history that was pre-registered at BIRTH. If this kid busts, Tim has to explain fantasy football to his son at every birthday. No pressure, Jeremiyah. Either of you.

A clean pick from the man who once traded Justin Herbert for DEREK CARR and change. That's not a trade, Kristian, that's identity theft where you steal the worse identity. Tate is talented enough that even you can't Carr him. Probably. 6-22 says don't tempt fate.

First of SEVEN Ben picks — a full teardown from the franchise that once traded Jalen Hurts for 2022 Russell Wilson, a move so cursed the Broncos are still apologizing for it. 8-20 wasn't bad luck, Ben. It was karma with a payment plan. Price is a real one though. Even karma respects volume.

Lee sprinted the card up like the building was on fire, which — when your superflex spot scored the second-fewest points in the league — it was. 9-19 with the offensive firepower of a participation trophy. Mendoza's the right pick. Being this correct this urgently is what desperation looks like when it showers.

The commissioner named his team after Ashton Jeanty, watched the RB run start, and drafted a wideout. But let's talk about the real shit, Aaron: you traded Saquon Barkley for Mike Evans and Rachaad White the season before Saquon ran for two thousand fucking yards and won a Super Bowl. You don't get to grade anyone's draft ever again. Concepcion's good. So was Saquon.

The reigning Toilet Bowl champion — a title you win by losing slower than six other losers — takes a QB. Alex's roster is a taxi squad with a rooftop bar: Cade Stover, Jawhar Jordan, Kalel Mullings, and now a ghost named Jonah Coleman that Sleeper won't even acknowledge. Simpson better be real, because half your franchise is legally hypothetical.

This is BRYAN'S old pick, and Tim used it on the NFL's 8th overall selection — who promptly showed up with a bad hamstring. An injured star arriving at the 1-27 franchise isn't a draft pick, it's hospice placement. Get well soon, Jordyn. Look what they did to the last 27 guys.

Life gave Lee a 9-19 season and the league's saddest scoreboard, so Lee drafted Lemon. The joke writes itself; the sadder part is the pick is genuinely good, which means the rebuild might work, which means we only have about a year of Maniacs jokes left. Cherish them.

The Coopers, who last offseason traded away Saquon AND Hurts in one deal and Tyreek in another, are now drafting rookies to replace the Hall of Fame wing they voluntarily demolished. Risky Business isn't a team name, it's a confession. Stribling's nice. So was the dynasty you dismantled for J.J. McCarthy.

Jacob once traded Saquon Barkley for KENYAN DRAKE, hung the most points in the league last year, and still owns zero trophies — the fantasy equivalent of a Ferrari that's never left the driveway. Now he's stapling a Jets receiver to the windshield. 1,756 points of 'almost,' and counting.

The most-traveled pick in league history lands on a tight end. Bryan turned this exact slot into James Cook and walked away whistling; Ben turned it into a TE2 lottery ticket for a team that won eight games. One of you two just got robbed, and Ben — buddy — the other guy's team is named after winning.

Lyndsey once traded Cooper Kupp for literally nothing — the season he won the receiving triple crown — and STILL owns more titles than the rest of you have excuses. That's not luck, that's a franchise so healthy it can eat a bullet and call it fiber. Stowers is a depth pick by someone who doesn't need any. Menacing.

1c.blurb: The Toilet Bowl prize, spent on a real NFL running back who — as of press time — exists on NO roster in Sleeper, because the platform doesn't know this pick exists and the commissioner hasn't entered him. Alex won the losers bracket and received a cryptid. Aaron, the man is a FREE AGENT right now. If someone snipes Coleman off waivers before you process this, the ensuing shitstorm will need its own constitutional convention, and The Oracle will testify against you.

2.blurb: David traded PATRICK MAHOMES in 2019 for a bag of Staffords, went 23-5 last year — best record ever recorded in this league — and lost the title anyway. This franchise also once benched 99 points in a playoff week, including Tom Brady. Emmett Johnson will be great for him from September through exactly Week 16, at which point the curse takes the wheel like it always does.

A back so anonymous the Oracle's own database didn't know him. Kristian scouting players the computers haven't indexed would be visionary from a contender; from a 6-22 team it's a man buying lottery tickets with his Herbert money. Still his Herbert money. Never forget.

Pick three of seven. Ben told Tim in the chat 'I normally bring hate your way' — bold trash talk from a man rebuilding out of a crater he dug himself, one Russell Wilson trade at a time. Bell's a solid brick. The house needed seven for a reason.

Lee grinding four picks into a roster that scored 1,300-something points is honest labor and the Oracle respects it. What it doesn't respect is that this franchise made ZERO trades of consequence in nine years and then wondered why the roster aged like milk. Bernard's fine. Pick up the phone sometime, Lee.

A Chiefs deep threat for the commissioner, who — reminder — got Mahomes off David for spare parts in 2019 and has been living off the interest ever since. Aaron's whole empire is other people's mistakes. Cyrus Allen is a fine dart. The Saquon trade is still on your permanent record.

Denzel Boston joins ghost-Coleman and the taxi squad screenplay. Alex's team-building strategy is casting a movie nobody greenlit: big names, no distribution deal, straight to the Toilet Bowl where it apparently wins awards.

Third pick for Tim, who has now added more talent in one afternoon than the 2025 Crab Boilers displayed in eighteen weeks. That's not a compliment to the draft, Tim. That's math about the season. One and twenty-seven. The Oracle counted twice.

This pick changed hands twice on draft day alone, which in the Cooper economy counts as barely used. A 6'4" Giants receiver acquired with laundered assets by the family that fenced Saquon. The IRS should look at this franchise. The talent evaluators shouldn't — the picks keep hitting, goddammit.

Singleton at 2.09 is theft, and everyone watching knew it, and nobody said anything because complaining about the Coopers getting value is the league's cardiovascular exercise. They sold the veterans, kept the receipts, and now the rookies keep falling to them. Infuriating. Five stars.

A red-zone Raven for the team that leads the league in points and trails it in jewelry. Jacob's title window has been propped open so long there are birds nesting in it. Lane catches touchdowns; the Meats catch feelings every December.

Steven. STEVEN. You traded JOSH ALLEN — the Josh Allen — in 2019 for a third and a fifth. That is the single worst transaction in the recorded history of this league, and possibly of commerce. Every pick you make for the rest of your life is measured against the MVP you gave away for pocket lint. Kaytron Allen is a nice player. He is not THAT Allen. Nothing ever will be.

Four of seven. The Dirty Birds bench once left 92 points sitting in a single week — twice in one season, actually, both 2019 — so hoarding this many rookies at least guarantees the future benching errors will involve exciting young talent. Growth, of a kind. Branch can fly. Somebody START him.

3.blurb: Fourth pick for the archaeological dig formerly known as a roster. Tim's draft is legitimately good, which the Oracle finds emotionally confusing, like watching the guy who failed the ACT ace the retake. Wait. Bad example. New data incoming, as the man says.

Five defensible picks in a row from Lee, whose franchise identity was previously 'sixth place in an eight-emotion league.' If the Maniacs actually get good, the Oracle loses a third of its material and Tim loses his only peer group. Selfishly: bust, please.

Pick five, a QB flier, standard ark-building. Somewhere in Denver, 2022 Russell Wilson nods approvingly at the Dirty Birds' continued faith in reclamation quarterbacks. Learn, Ben. The stove is STILL hot.
A man named Ted, drafted in round three by a chop shop with a straight face. The Coopers have earned the benefit of the doubt and it makes everyone sick. Godspeed, Ted. You're evidence now.

Sneaky-good pick from the Josh Allen fugitive. Steven's rap sheet has one felony on it, but it's a big one, so every quiet value grab like this reads as community service. Roughly forty more of these and you're even, Steven. That's the math on an MVP.

Another cast member for Alex's straight-to-Toilet-Bowl production. At some point a team full of great names has to score fantasy points, but that's a problem for whichever version of this roster Sleeper decides is real.

SIX. This is Bryan's old 3.07, by the way — sold off in the Cook heist — now converted into a lanky Panther by a man stockpiling rookies like the apocalypse is position-scarce. The Birds drafted almost as many players tonight as games they won last year. That sentence should hurt. It's supposed to.

David hoarding QBs seven years after handing Mahomes to the commissioner is the saddest redemption arc in the league — a man installing smoke detectors in every room of a house that already burned down. Allar's a fine stash. The Brady bench points remain unrecovered.
A Patriots tight end: the fantasy position where hope files for unemployment. Lee's sixth pick of a genuinely industrious rebuild, and the first one the Oracle would quietly leave at the airport.

The commissioner drafts a Dolphin while an undrafted cryptid named Jonah Coleman wanders the waiver wire OUTSIDE his own league's database. Priorities, Aaron. The Oracle has filed a formal complaint with itself.
A second QB in four picks. David, we see you. Everyone sees you. The Mahomes-shaped hole doesn't fill from the outside, buddy — that's therapy, and the co-pay is cheaper than a 2027 second.

The champ drafts a bowling-ball Raven with the bored precision of a poker player who already knows the river card. Gave away Kupp, gave away McCaffrey, kept winning anyway. Some franchises are protected by the football gods; this one has them on retainer.

4.blurb: A Jets QB to open round four, drafted by a man whose QB room already contains Mahomes AND Watson — one all-time heist and one all-time hostage situation, both acquired on purpose. Aaron's roster is a museum of other people's regret with a gift shop.

Kristian drafts the alphabet's final boss. A 6-22 team stashing a third QB named Kaliakmanis is either 4-D chess or a cry for help in Greek, and given the Herbert-for-Carr precedent, the Oracle knows which way it's leaning.

SEVEN. Ben drafted nearly as many humans tonight as wins last season, and the haul — Price, Sadiq, Bell, Branch, Beck, Brazzell, Delp — is honestly excellent, which is the most annoying possible outcome for everyone who wanted to keep laughing. Congratulations, asshole. Now start the right ones — 2019's benches are still bleeding.

Drafting a guy named Lance in the fourth is walking under a ladder on purpose, but at pick seven-of-the-night for a rebuilding team it's house money. Lee did more work tonight than the 2025 Maniacs did all November. Verifiably. The Oracle checked November.

Jonathan Taylor's direct handcuff — a back Taylor personally compared to David Montgomery — falls to 4.05 and Steven just... takes him. Quietly. The best value of the round to the man with no team name and one unforgivable sin. The Josh Allen debt shrinks by a nickel. Only nineteen dollars and ninety-five cents to go.

An Eagles QB named like a Madden create-a-player, joining a roster that's 40% fictional. Between the ghost, the screenplay names, and a Toilet Bowl title, Alex's franchise is the league's first magical-realism entry. García Márquez would've gone 6-8 too.

And here's the smuggest man in Ohio — who, full disclosure, traded CeeDee Lamb for Trey Benson and Jaxson Dart last fall, so hold the coronation. Bryan gutted his entire draft for James Cook and Rico Dowdle, showed up for ONE pick like it was jury duty, and threw it at a D-II folk hero currently terrorizing Atlanta's depth chart. If Strand hits, unbearable. If he doesn't, still got Cook, still unbearable. The Lamb trade is the only thing keeping this man humble and he's ALREADY not.

A legit athletic TE at 4.08 because of course he fell to them. The Coopers finish with five picks of actual substance while the league mutters into its beer. Somebody audit these brothers. Find the second set of books.

And a Raiders burner to garnish it. Risky Business walked out with the deepest class in the room a year after selling three superstars — the full pawn-shop cycle, executed clean. It shouldn't work. It keeps working. The Oracle is legally required to be impressed and personally chooses to be irritated.

More speed for the fastest team to never finish first. Jacob, you traded Saquon for Kenyan Drake once — the window has forgiven you, the scoreboard has forgiven you, ONE BANNER would forgive everything. Climb through the goddamn window before it paints itself shut.

Lee's seventh pick, tying Ben for volume, on a Steeler that spellcheck will fight until Christmas. Two franchises drafted half the class tonight; only one of them told the other 'I normally bring hate your way' in the chat first. Rebuilds with beef. The Oracle approves.

Mr. Irrelevant is a Jaguars tight end, taken by the champ, who did nothing all night and leaves the favorite anyway — the same franchise that gave away Kupp AND McCaffrey and lapped everyone regardless. The rest of you traded MVPs for magic beans; Lyndsey planted the beans and grew a fucking dynasty. See everyone in Week 1. Bring the Toilet Bowl brackets.

awards.why: Seven picks, real talent throughout, and the self-awareness to admit 8-20 needed dynamite. The Russell Wilson trade is almost forgiven. Almost.
Jonathan Taylor's handcuff in the fourth round. First recorded instance of Steven being on the RIGHT side of a heist since he handed Josh Allen away for a third and a fifth.
One pick all night, spent on an undrafted D-II legend. All gas, no draft. The CeeDee Lamb trade watches silently from the corner.
Drafted with a pick Sleeper doesn't track, currently rostered by nobody, findable on waivers. AARON. THE MAN IS LOOSE.
NFL 8th overall, hamstring already barking, delivered to the 1-27 franchise. Flowers are being accepted in lieu of fantasy points.
Named his son Jeremiayah Love in July. Drafted Jeremiyah Love in August. The first pick ever scouted in a delivery room.
Three depth picks, zero urgency, still the favorite. Traded away Kupp and McCaffrey in her career and won titles anyway. The house always wins; Lyndsey IS the house.
